newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian bonds lower, fixated by possible Buba move.
newsitem.headline: Belgian bonds lower, fixated by possible Buba move.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds declined in morning business on Monday on a followthrough to Friday's U.S.-led sell-off and amid speculation that the German central bank might tinker with the repo rate on Thursday, traders said.
"There is essentially no change from Friday. We are trading lower with Bunds," one trader said. "But the market is also finally realising that the Buba might do something on Thursday."
There has been speculation for the past two weeks that the Bundesbank might announce either a variable repo rate -- a de facto rate rise -- or possibly introduce a two-tier repo later this week.
Traders said such a move on the German repo was not fully priced into the Belgian bond market.
"The short end remains very vulnerable. If the Buba does bring in a variable repo there will be a massacre," one said.
Traders said Tuesday's OLO exchange auction was also a focus of attention.

On Tuesday the Belgian Treasury will offer OLO 27 (4.00 pct, January 2000), OLO 10 (8.75 pct, June 2002), OLO 19 (6.50 pct, March 2005), and OLO 16 (7.50 pct, July 2008) in exchange for OLO 8 (9.25 pct, August 1997) and OLO 4 (9.25 pct, January 1998).
Money market rates were little changed from Friday.
The one-week repo was 3.58/64 percent against 3.55/65, and the franc/mark exchange rate was 20.6470/85 against 20.6455/85.
However, traders said they expected the down trend in money rates, which started in the middle of last week after a sudden spurt above 4.00 percent, to once again turn into a rise next week.
At 0900 GMT on Monday the yield of the benchmark 10-year OLO was 5.70 percent against Friday's closing 5.68, and the spread over Bunds was static at eight basis points.
Traders said they expected the spread to fluctuate between nine and 14 basis points.
The front month futures contract was 18 basis points lower at 121.31.
Traders said the focus of activity was the long end of the yield curve.
"People have finally woken up. The long end is extremely well bid," one said.
